summary: Check logs the full rejected token with %q. Rejected tokens are often real credentials: expired or revoked tokens, tokens rejected by clock skew, or a valid token sent to the wrong environment. Writing them into server logs leaks secrets to everyone with log access, and the review plan's secrets check rules it out. The story only needs the reason, which err already carries. Otherwise the behaviour matches both criteria.

findings.title: Rejected API token is written verbatim to the log
findings.detail: The raw token string is logged on every rejection. API tokens are bearer secrets, and rejected ones are frequently still sensitive or valid elsewhere (expired-but-refreshable, revoked after leak, wrong-environment, transient parse failure). Logs are retained, shipped to aggregators and read by support, so this turns the log pipeline into a credential store. The story asks only for the reason, which err provides.
findings.fix: Log only the reason and a non-reversible identifier, for example log.Printf("auth: rejected token (sha256 prefix %s): %v", fingerprint(token), err), where fingerprint returns the first 8 hex chars of a SHA-256. Alternatively log just err and the token's key ID or subject if parse can extract it safely. Add a test that captures log output and asserts the token does not appear.

criteria.evidence: verify.go:22-24 returns ErrUnauthorized and logs err (the reason) on a parse failure; TestCheckRejects asserts errors.Is(err, ErrUnauthorized). The log line also leaks the token (finding).
verify.go:21,26: when parse succeeds, Check returns its claims and nil. No test covers the valid path, but the code is direct.
